text:
ryan_csm: FYI — new tenant (AcmeEdge) onboarded today. Their traffic is tiny most hours but explodes in short bursts (10–20x) during regional shifts. Need a short, customer-facing runbook we can hand to the CSM + ops to reduce cold-start pain and show renewal signal coverage. Any compact pattern for caching/batching/streaming for this edge-case? :wave:

maria_cs: Short checklist idea: 1) micro-warm pools, 2) adaptive batch windows, 3) client-side jitter + backoff guidance, 4) clear fallback expectations for the customer. Keep it 1 page.

jamal_se: Agree. Technical bits: use small persistent warm pool (1–2 GPUs) for that tenant during predicted surge windows, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, and set batching target low latency for small bursts. Also recommend client-side concurrency limit of 5.

oliver_sre: Also add a telemetry hook: capture tenant spike ratio (burst_count / avg_minute) and flag when >8 for 3 windows — triggers manual warm pool. We'll add a runbook step to flip the warm pool toggle. :gear:

sara_pm: Can we make the runbook customer-facing (one-pager) + internal ops checklist? Customer-facing should say "expected behavior during bursts" and include explicit SLA-ish guidance (e.g., degraded throughput might happen for 30–90s while warm pool spins up). Keep language non-technical.

ryan_csm: Love that. We also need renewal-risk signals in the runbook so CSMs escalate early: repeated >3 burst timeouts in 7 days, >50% drop in success rate, or repeated support requests mentioning latency. That should map to an "engage" play.

maria_cs: I'll draft the customer-facing snippet. Suggest wording: "To improve responsiveness during sudden spikes we recommend enabling our Micro-Warm option and following the lightweight client guidance below." Then include a tiny checklist.

jamal_se: Example lightweight config we can paste into the runbook for the SRE/Dev team (internal):

```json
{
  "warm_pool": {
    "enabled": true,
    "min_workers": 2,
    "scale_up_threshold": 8,
    "scale_up_window_sec": 30
  },
  "batching": {
    "max_batch_size": 8,
    "max_wait_ms": 40
  },
  "cache": {
    "prefix_cache_ttl_sec": 300,
    "kv_cache_enabled": true
  }
}
```

jamal_se: That config is intentionally conservative for bursty tenants; adjust numbers after 72h telemetry.

oliver_sre: Operational notes to add: - Canary the warm pool during low-traffic windows first. - Add a rollback plan: if CPU/GPU error rate spikes by 5% within 10m, disable warm pool and notify CSM. - Add cost-impact line for customer-facing doc.

deploy-bot: Reminder: please link to runbook stub -> https://redwood-internal/runbooks/cs/edge-warmup (draft created).

sara_pm: For enablement coordination: CSM should run a 15-min sync with the customer's dev lead before first predicted surge. Agenda: confirm client concurrency limits, confirm sample prompt distribution, set monitoring alert thresholds, and agree on rollback contact.

ryan_csm: Also add feedback capture: short post-surge survey we send 1h after major burst: 3 Qs (latency ok?, any errors?, overall satisfaction 1–5). Tie responses into renewal-risk dashboard.

maria_cs: I'll write the one-pager and the 3-question survey template. Quick draft Qs: 1) "Did you notice slower responses during the spike?" 2) "Any errors or failed requests? (brief)" 3) "Overall satisfaction 1–5". Keep it optional but recommended.

oliver_sre: Metrics to show on the CSM-facing dashboard: p50/p95 latency, cold-start count, warm-pool on/off, burst_count, error_rate, survey responses. Add a small visual for before/after warm pool.

jamal_se: One more client recommendation: add lightweight client-side caching for repeated identical prompts with TTL 60s and tie it to conversational session ids. That reduces hot-key pressure.

ryan_csm: Next steps: @maria_cs draft one-pager + survey; @jamal_se paste config into internal runbook and add scale knobs; @oliver_sre wire telemetry flags and dashboard card; @sara_pm add the 15-min sync agenda to CSM playbook. Target: draft to stakeholders in 48h. :thumbsup:

maria_cs: On it — I'll post draft by EOD tomorrow.

jamal_se: I'll commit the config to the runbook branch and open a PR.

oliver_sre: I'll add alerts + dashboard widget, will ping when ready for review.

sara_pm: I'll update the enablement checklist with the sync agenda and a suggested script.

ryan_csm: Thanks all — this should give the customer clear expectations and protect renewal. I'll close the loop with AcmeEdge after we share the one-pager. :rocket:
